short_summary: East Java's capital is renowned for distinctive cuisine, historic architecture, and role as Indonesia's second-busiest seaport.
method_note: Agent reported WebFetch unavailable · evidence from WebSearch result snippets. Strong Wikipedia + travel guide mix.

food.claim: Rawon, a black beef soup made with keluak nut, rated world's best soup by TasteAtlas in 2024.
Rujak cingur, signature Surabaya salad using cow's mouth with fried tempeh, tofu, and vegetables.
Lontong balap, street food of compressed rice cakes with bean sprouts and shrimp paste, originating in 1950s Surabaya.

shopping.claim: Pasar Pabean, indoor seafood market linking Arab Quarter and Chinatown with fresh catches from Madura Strait.
Tunjungan Plaza, East Java's largest mall with 52-story tower containing 500+ stores and international brands.

attractions.claim: House of Sampoerna, 19th-century Dutch building showcasing traditional hand-rolled clove cigarette manufacturing.
Heroes Monument, 41-meter obelisk commemorating November 10, 1945 battle with attached museum and memorial park.
Ampel, historic Arab Quarter centered on Sunan Ampel mosque with Middle Eastern cuisine and coffee shops.
Chinatown near Old Town, featuring atmospheric streets and Hong Tiek Hian Temple, one of Surabaya's oldest Chinese temples.

transport.claim: Juanda International Airport, major gateway with taxi service to city center taking 17 minutes.
Gubeng Station, central railway hub serving east, south and west destinations via Java's southern line.
Pasar Turi Station, northwestern railway hub opened 1900, serving Jakarta and Semarang via Java's northern line.
Port of Tanjung Perak, Indonesia's second-busiest seaport connecting Southeast Asia, East Asia, and global trade networks.
